event.canonical_title: Michigan Democrats Select Senate Nominee Amid Record Spending and Party Divisions
event.summary: Michigan Democrats are voting in a Senate primary featuring Rep. Haley Stevens and Abdul El-Sayed. The race has garnered significant attention due to record financial contributions, particularly from pro-Israel groups, totaling around $30 million. The candidates represent differing views on U.S.-Israel relations and the future direction of the Democratic Party, highlighting a divide within the party.

timeline.title: El-Sayed Maintains Narrow Lead in Michigan Senate Primary Against Stevens
timeline.summary: In a closely contested Democratic Senate primary in Michigan, Abdul El-Sayed is holding a narrow lead over Haley Stevens as votes continue to be counted. The race has been characterized as a significant test for the Democratic Party's direction, with El-Sayed emphasizing the need for unity among Democrats following the hard-fought contest.

The race is described as tight and significant for the Democratic Party's future.
El-Sayed has called for unity among Democrats after the primary.

event_overview.title: About Michigan Senate Primary
event_overview.subject: Michigan Senate Primary
event_overview.summary: The Michigan Senate primary is the August 4, 2026 statewide nomination contest for one of Michigan’s U.S. Senate seats. It determined each major party’s nominee for the November 3 general election, when voters will choose a senator for a six-year term.

facts.label: Primary date and jurisdiction
facts.value: The statewide primary election was held in Michigan on Tuesday, August 4, 2026.

facts.label: Office at stake
facts.value: The ballot included one statewide U.S. Senate position with a six-year term; each state has two U.S. senators.

facts.label: Democratic primary field
facts.value: Michigan’s official candidate listing named Abdul El-Sayed, Mallory McMorrow, and Haley Stevens as Democratic candidates for U.S. Senate.

facts.label: Republican primary field
facts.value: Michigan’s official candidate listing named Mike Rogers as the Republican U.S. Senate candidate; Bernadette Smith was listed as disqualified.

facts.label: Election format and next stage
facts.value: Michigan’s August primary is for eligible Democratic and Republican candidates, and the winning nominees advance to the November general-election ballot. The 2026 general election is scheduled for November 3.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the Democratic nomination contest and its immediate vote-counting developments, not the full set of Michigan primary races, the Republican nomination process, or the November general-election campaign.
